items.title: Mrs. Francis Oliver Interview, 1969-05-10
items.q: My grandmother wanted us to be housewives.

ctx.x: of her, too. Did you have a piano in your grandmother's home? No. I wonder. No. Or any other instruments around? No, not that I can remember. Did you ever learn any music? I know you were

interested in music. I did, but I never did learn anything. My grandmother wanted us to be housewives. She taught us how to cook, sew, wash, and take care of babies. She felt like marriage is an institution as well as Annie. Yeah. Well, my grandson plays music now. He's a pianist, and he had—I gave him a piano when he was 12. So he's doing nicely with his music, too. He's 17 now. I'm just hoping that one of them would have something that my brother had, you know what I mean? Some of that challenge. Some of that…
I mean? Yes, yes. I studied music. That's all I ever played was classics. Yes. But I got interested in the—
